title: Show recovery guidance when startup storage cannot open
description: lib/main.dart opens sensor_records, rgb_lighting, and preferences before runApp without handling failures. User debug launch failed with errno 11 locking /home/prnice/Documents/sensor_records.lock and displayed a black window. Existing AppImage PID 1077994 (started 2026-11-17 11:22) still holds matching preferences and rgb_lighting lock inodes; sensor_records.lock was absent at inspection. Add a visible startup failure state with actionable guidance and safe retry/close behavior. Preserve data and file locking; do not delete locks or bypass exclusive access. Verify lock contention between two processes and successful retry after owner exits.
notes:
Implementing visible storage recovery on deployment/release-readiness. Cause is known: unhandled Hive open/lock failure before runApp. Scope is retry/close and partial-open cleanup with real lock-contention verification; this is separate from deferred native shutdown research.
2026-11-17 bounded implementation rejected after real contention review. Initial agent test released the owner before opening, so its passing result did not verify locking. Corrected test attempted bootstrap.open while a separate Dart process still held sensor_records: FileSystemException occurred, then the assertion that sensor_records.lock still exists failed. Hive CE 2.23.3 hive_impl.dart failed-open cleanup calls newBox.close; storage_backend_vm.dart initialize line126 acquires lock, but _closeInternal line309 deletes the path even after failed acquisition. Retry could create a new pathname/inode and bypass the existing owner lock. pub.dev API still identifies 2.23.3 as latest stable. No dependency override, custom lock mechanism, or recovery code is shipped. Original app code restored. Durable diagnosis/sequence in docs/startup-storage.md; retained rejected patch/files/log under /tmp/opencode/startup-recovery-rejected* and /tmp/opencode/startup-lock-verification.log with hashes in docs. Resume only after a supported fix preserves the existing owner lock across failed/repeated opens, then prove retry after owner exit and retained values. No native crash work resumed.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text:
# Flutter shutdown patch audit

Baseline: Flutter framework `ab2912035e160d9cad6306df307576da6128ebdb`,
engine.version `371f77202a73e8dff57a8b3bff75bca55c090aee`, app baseline `77a189e`.

## Pinned upstream PRs

| PR | state | head | merge | base | patch SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 193533 | open | `abacb7417205339cd75ad09e55b8e6063a983ec0` | `155c295604f732f3319de5add73438c156ee1aef` (current merge ref) | `8a756b221888d4d63892d5aa90a6eca884ef5393` | `fdeab6e4807a57c7d6f5fd3a8a92a88cf7c0c7f607dd5efe4f8a3531a61e3463`
| 193126 | open | `34067b1a6e2c5121dbaf5915517f989c2f48fe68` | `069b44ee5b1090fa10f1ca07df1c0c1d065b9173` | `abacb7417205339cd75ad09e55b8e6063a983ec0` (PR193533 head) | `c165e743312b222dd8ec8cd5535923a3615310419d33f226ce7d735e25a765c8`
| 194525 | merged | `aeb1406c38318689041e33782589c8da2b8394c8` | `cb1b233755444fd7d2e84bda6971aecff1692c1e1` | `9cba7392c62645f790ccd8c2efda0a6658d260d7` | `738be5d5000ea9f9e47965d1fc1ff1caa0d43cab8b344c468a5c0dd6380d027b`

PR193533 is the required first patch; PR193126 is based directly on its head.
PR194525 applies after that pair in the current Flutter checkout. In an isolated
checkout, `git apply --check` passed for 193533 then 193126 on base
`8a756b...`, and passed for 194525 after the pair. PR194525 also applies to the
3.50 framework checkout because its task-runner context is older-compatible.
PR193533 did not apply cleanly to exact 3.50: the source changes matched except
for `engine/src/.../testing/mock_gtk.cc`; PR193126 cannot apply independently
because it requires 193533. This is an upstream test-helper/context conflict,
not evidence that the engine changes are compatible with engine revision
`371f...`; builder must resolve it in the isolated source tree and record the
result. No app or shared SDK files were changed.

## Lifecycle finding

Exact stock Linux source `fl_platform_handler.cc::quit_application()` detaches
GTK application windows and calls `g_application_quit()`. It does not stop or
join the Flutter engine/raster worker. `fl_engine_dispose()` eventually calls
embedder `Shutdown`, but only when the last `FlEngine` reference is disposed.
The app deliberately retains that reference in `linux/runner/my_application.cc`
(`g_set_object(&self->engine, fl_view_get_engine(view))`) and clears it in
`my_application_dispose()`, after `g_application_run()` returns (`main.cc` owns
`g_autoptr(MyApplication)`).

PR193533 retains renderer/task-runner/mutex lifetime and serializes OpenGL
resource cleanup against `present_layers()`. PR193126 cancels an active GTK
`wait_for_frame` and defers secondary GTK window destruction. PR194525 fixes a
`FlTaskRunner` timeout-source use-after-free. None calls an engine stop/join,
waits for the Flutter raster thread, or changes `quit_application()` /
`fl_engine_dispose()` ordering. They target secondary-window/renderer and task
runner teardown, not the observed main-thread `exit` versus `io.flutter.rast`
LLVM/Mesa overlap.

## Recommended experiment

1. Build the smallest ordered engine candidate: 193533 -> 193126 -> 194525,
   with framework changes only where required by the patches. First test the
   unchanged app, including its retained `FlEngine`, under the standard launch
   and repeated X11/Wayland close/exit checks.
2. Do not repeat the old forced `gtk_widget_destroy`/`g_object_run_dispose`
   experiment against stock. PR193533 changes the exact renderer reference and
   `frame_mutex` invariant that made that forced path abort, but it still does
   not provide process-exit synchronization and would confound the root test.
3. Only if the patched engine's normal lifecycle is clean, run a separate
   app-variant trial removing the temporary `MyApplication::engine` retention.
   Let the normal `GApplication`/GTK destruction path run; do not add a custom
   launcher, `_Exit`, renderer flags, or private API. Treat this as an ownership
   probe, not a fix: dropping the reference earlier may make `FlEngine` shutdown
   occur before process exit, but the patches do not prove that it joins the
   raster worker.

Expected interpretation: a clean unchanged-app result establishes renderer
teardown compatibility only. A clean no-retention result is the first evidence
that normal final reference disposal changes this app's exit race. Neither is a
confirmed root fix until repeated close and exit captures show no surviving
raster worker at process exit.

The isolated experiment built and tested both variants with fresh release/AOT.
It does not establish a production fix. Removing application engine retention
(B) is rejected by a first-close Ubuntu abort. Keeping retention (A) completed
the bounded local checks, but shutdown ordering remains unknown.

| A: retained engine | 20/20 normal closes; installation, helper approval/denial/missing-agent, readback/restore, upgrade and purge passed | Two functional closes, ten X11 closes and ten Wayland closes passed; denial, approved retry, readback/restore and helper cleanup passed |
| B: normal reference ownership | Dashboard after 2.5s; first close aborted (`-6`); 0/1 closes passed, remaining 19 and later helper/upgrade/purge checks did not run | The same complete 22-close functional/X11/Wayland flow passed |

Both platforms proved approved-user core capture before app launch. No app
failure was rerun. The prior stock hosted core remains the baseline; no new
stock repetitions ran. No engine lifecycle tracing was added.

## Exact inputs

- App base: `77a189e1e4620d544a85509b3417fc91f3800156`
- A package source: `61367a98775765d1144f2d9bd50a1a124a1ce7df`

  the full patches and the test-only MockGtk conflict adaptation.

and pub cache were copied privately for A and B; exported engine outputs were

the supported local-engine flags, fresh kernel/AOT, and existing package staging.
The source companions include the export manifest, source archive, provenance,
local-engine arguments and explicit experimental/non-release fields. Neither a
stock manifest nor old AOT was reused. All four shipped runtimes match the hash
above. The SDK's Git-derived prerelease-looking version is not a source roll or
runtime identity.

The original engine native result remains 83/84. The separate AT-SPI report
classifies its failure and records one unchanged test passing in a complete
environment; it does not replace that result with 84/84. See
`/tmp/opencode/flutter-shutdown-engine-experiment/atk-investigation/report.md`.

## B's first Ubuntu failure

The app logged `bad_alloc was thrown in -fno-exceptions mode`. The saved
systemd all-thread report identifies raster LWP 4237:

```text
abort
std::__fl::__libcpp_verbose_abort
std::__throw_bad_alloc
operator new
llvm::TargetPassConfig::addPass
LLVM machine-pass setup / MCJIT finalization
LLVMGetPointerToGlobal
swrast_dri.so
impeller::RenderPassGLES / ReactorGLES
Flutter Rasterizer
```

Main LWP 4213 was concurrently in `libLLVM-15.so.1` from libc `exit`. This
retains the process-exit/raster overlap seen in the stock core, but the signal
and immediate fault differ. It does not prove an OS OOM, a particular allocation
size, or that these patches caused the failure. No app/plugin frame appears in
the faulting chain. Removing the extra reference did not reliably stop raster
work before process exit.

files. Qualification status remained 1; collection status 1; archive status 0.

An offline GDB command, with automatic host-library loading disabled, completed
and saved core mappings and raw all-thread addresses under `B/offline-core/`.
The core's own systemd report supplies matching library build IDs and the
symbolized failing chain. Attempts to fetch the exact old libc package returned
404; no mismatched newer libc was substituted for symbolization. No app reran.
Systemd report SHA256: `c038e1a7b095c95a593f47ca48b25391cdb6f8d5d2223bfc82b78cd2254d00cb`.
Offline raw-address/mappings SHA256: `515c90f29c0e7d2275cf232dcf532316592e8b90224fd355ddbb884777d9c741`.

## Environments and instrumentation

Local KVM host: AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, Linux `7.3.1`, host QEMU `11.1.2`.
Ubuntu guest: 22.04.5, kernel `5.15.0-203-generic`, Mesa
`23.2.1-1ubuntu3.1~22.04.4`, LLVM `15.0.7-0ubuntu0.22.04.3`.
NixOS guests: kernel `6.18.60`, same guest-visible CPU; exact Nixpkgs is pinned
by the harness branch's unchanged flake.lock.

The harness is branch `experiment/shutdown-acceptance`. Ubuntu used `bc297ee`;
NixOS used `8a977b5`. PR 10's fixture/core instrumentation was reused. NixOS
adds only guest coredump/GDB tooling, core limits and accessibility service
provisioning; its standard appimage-run namespace and authorization checks stay
intact. The NixOS assertion migration was fixed before either app launched.

AT-SPI service provisioning was explicit: Ubuntu added `at-spi2-core`; NixOS
provided the same standard service through its package/D-Bus configuration.
Existing private D-Bus sessions remain in use; no critical was filtered and no
`NO_AT_BRIDGE` or module override was set. Ubuntu's inherited root
`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` produced dconf warnings in accessibility-service subprocesses.
Those warnings remain in the logs. App close/GLib-critical gates passed for A;
this environmental imperfection was not silently repaired by rerunning it.

All Docker commands used `--init`; builds had a 45-minute outer bound and
bounded cleanup. Ubuntu VM commands had a 35-minute bound; NixOS commands had a
50-minute bound. None reached those bounds. Failed prerequisites/logs remain:
the first B build could not see external worktree Git metadata, and the first
NixOS A evaluation used the removed coredump option. Both were fixed before app
execution. They are not app retries.

## Commands, checks and limits

Per variant, the build entry was:

```bash
bash tool/build_experimental_packages.sh A_or_B deb PRIVATE_CONSUMER NEW_OUTPUT
bash tool/build_experimental_packages.sh A_or_B appimage PRIVATE_CONSUMER NEW_OUTPUT
```

The driver and package sources at the recorded commits contain the complete
Docker mounts, environment, local-engine arguments, hashes and build steps.
The acceptance entries were the standard VM runner with
`LLLF_VM_ACCELERATOR=kvm LLLF_DEB_CORE_DIAGNOSTIC_ATTEMPTS=20` and the standard
`tool/test_appimage_nixos.sh` with the derived AppImage.

Additional gates: 16 packaging tests passed, focused Dart analysis found no
issues, shell/Python/Nix syntax and ShellCheck checks passed, and the app
lockfile/launchers remained unchanged. These tool tests used a private SDK's
ordinary cached test engine; they are not patched-engine native tests.

Evidence root: `/tmp/opencode/lllf-shutdown-results/`. `results.json` records
artifact/source/AOT hashes and verified counts; `SHA256SUMS` fingerprints the
retained artifacts and logs. Successful NixOS outputs and fixture cores are
copied locally as well as retained by their result links.

No hosted run, full Flutter suite, real-hardware password cancellation, full
engine native suite, or lifecycle-order tracing ran here. A's local passes are
bounded non-reproduction, not proof of shutdown synchronization. B fails the
required matrix and is not a fix. No production fix or custom-engine adoption
is justified. Parent review is needed before a hosted A comparison or further
ordering diagnostics. PR 9, main, shared SDK, export, and published/convenience
artifacts remain unchanged.

comments.text: Infrastructure hypothesis for parent workflow owner: all portable distro VMs in run 43718830751 printed 'tcg, CPU Nehalem'. tool/test_portable_distro.sh selects KVM only when /dev/kvm is readable and writable; Debian job does not run cachix/install-nix-action before its VM tests, while AppImage runs it only after the Ubuntu VM. # Official Flutter 3.50 Debian 12 qualification

## Result

The exact official package from CI `43726942646` passed the missing Debian 12
qualification in a local disposable KVM guest. This is new platform coverage,
not a retry of the failed Ubuntu phase. No app or package was rebuilt.

- Dashboard rendered after 1.9 seconds.
- The single ordinary normal close exited zero. No 20-close loop ran.
- Installation/payload verification, helper approval, denial, missing agent,
  readback/restoration, upgrade, purge, and existing-integration preservation
  all passed.
- Qualification, collection, and archive statuses were zero.
- Before app launch, the approved-user controlled abort proved unlimited soft
  and hard core limits, retained its raw SIGABRT core, and produced a GDB
  backtrace and mappings. Both GDB status fields were zero.
- No app failure/core occurred. The only core was the controlled fixture.

The original Ubuntu 22.04 normal-close failure remains unresolved. This local
Debian 12 result does not turn the failed CI run green or establish a shutdown
fix. The user-reported working official AppImage and authentication retry are
separate evidence; real-hardware readback/restoration remain unreported here.

## Exact official inputs

- Package SHA256: `3b169c4d1fe8cb684c958363ded0a43b399b1dfed226e390ef023af06a85bae2`

title: Contain portable backend processes and helper lifetime
description: Scope control/legion_control_service.cc ActiveOperation, invoke, operation_timeout, sender-disconnect and shutdown paths; future portable helper supervision. Current g_subprocess_force_exit terminates only the immediate child; descendant processes retaining output pipes can outlive disconnect/timeout and prevent completion. Design bounded whole-process-tree containment without PID-reuse races; cover crash, SIGKILL of UI/launcher, descendant holding stdout, stalled auth/startup, multiple instances, temporary payload cleanup, and helper idle timeout. Use hardware-free fixtures. Do not enable portable hardware writes before these lifecycle gates pass.
design: Use one systemd transient service per validated backend operation. Manager-owned cgroups contain setsid/double-fork descendants; RuntimeMaxUSec is independent of helper liveness. Bind operation to parent helper service with BindsTo/After and share PrivateTmp via JoinsNamespaceOf to preserve payload visibility. Keep hardening, PATH and typed allow-list. Pin manager owner, AddRef until exit status captured, then UnrefUnit and collect; cancellation waits for the start reply before stopping. Uncertain cleanup fails closed. Portable root helper will also need a transient service lifetime (no installed files). Verify actual kernel containment in a disposable QEMU NixOS VM, never on the host manager.

title: Prevent NVIDIA CDI regeneration from blocking iGPU-only hibernate resume
description: Normal graphical-session hibernate restored the same boot and desktop/audio, but the NVIDIA udev rule restarted nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator.service while user.slice was frozen. Its nvidia-ctk process held NVIDIA devices at the second reconciliation attempt, causing the hook to reject clients and thaw with NVIDIA attached. The current ExecCondition checks only PCI presence and passes during transient resume re-enumeration. Gate CDI generation on authoritative expected attached policy as well as NVIDIA PCI presence; retain strict reconciliation client rejection.

title: Guard suspend-then-hibernate with authoritative detached graphics preflight
description: The pending lifecycle preflight is ordered before systemd-hibernate.service only. The configured lid path uses systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service, which bypasses that guard even though the post hook handles its hibernate phase. Design and validate a guard sufficiently close to the actual hibernate transition; a check only before the initial suspend may become stale. Keep this path outside the direct-hibernate validation claim.
notes:
2026-09-09 deployment verified on the running system (generation a83lrj7pxxhjdvpvkdhhha07zkk2b4ci, 20260908.d6524aa). The suspend-then-hibernate drop-in overrides ExecStart with the patched f7sif91nk1vk3zfial5j13km478i7hbp-legion-systemd-sleep-261.2, which embeds the djn4zffj6fzgipfhzdgs5ia0j7vvsdr2 preflight wrapper. The preflight is Before and required by both systemd-hibernate.service and systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service. The rendered wrapper passes its real timeout/exit-propagation test. Authoritative user-run root status: complete inspection, zero clients, detached/settled. System running with zero failed units and unchanged shutdown-mode sleep config. Hardware validation of the s2h path remains pending: manual-wake-before-delay test first, then a timer-driven hibernate transition with journal evidence and post-resume graphics/desktop/audio/Wi-Fi verification.
2026-09-09 root cause found for suspend-then-hibernate never sleeping: hosts/nixos/hardware/hibernate.nix defined empty nvidia-suspend/nvidia-resume ordering shims (no ExecStart) with requiredBy/wantedBy on systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service. systemd 261.2 refuses empty services (Service has no ExecStart=, ExecStop=, or SuccessAction=. Refusing), so each s2h job failed with 'Unit nvidia-suspend.service has a bad unit file setting' before any suspend. Direct suspend and hibernate were unaffected because they do not require that unit. With NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1 (open modules + 595 default) these units are ordering-only, so both now use Type=oneshot with ExecStart=coreutils true. Host build passed (vlxsalhsphhyf67ddpw22jmd6b0xlqjl) with the valid units and preserved s2h requires symlinks. One normal-suspend attempt also hit a transient EBUSY right after wlo1 deauthentication (mt7921e in-flight state); a retry succeeded. Hardware validation pending user switch and retest.
2026-09-09 manual-wake validation PASSED at monotonic 129776-129782 after switch deployed the no-op nvidia-suspend fix: nvidia-suspend.service started and deactivated successfully, entry preflight reported complete zero-client detached/settled inspection, system suspended ~1s, user woke manually, no hibernate attempt occurred (correct for wake before HibernateDelaySec), user.slice thawed, service finished with zero failed units, and graphics remains detached/settled. Remaining: timer-driven transition test (30-minute delay or a temporary shortened HibernateDelaySec reverted afterward) to validate the second preflight between suspend return and hibernate write, followed by same-image restore verification.
close_reason: Manual-wake and timer-driven suspend-then-hibernate cycles both validated after the nvidia-suspend no-op fix: entry preflight, patched-binary second preflight between suspend return and hibernate write, same-image restore (boot a4af09f3), post-resume reconciliation to detached/settled with complete zero-client inspection before user.slice thaw, desktop/audio/Wi-Fi recovered automatically, zero failed units, sleep config and PM diagnostics restored. Recurring mt7921e and NVIDIA-assertion issues remain separately tracked.

title: Reconcile dGPU after iGPU-only hibernate resume
description: Shutdown-mode hibernation from settled hybrid-igpu-only successfully wrote and restored the same kernel image, but firmware/hardware reset made the NVIDIA PCI functions reappear during kernel device restoration. NVIDIA DRM loaded before systemd's post-sleep hooks and before user.slice thaw. Reconcile the persisted iGPU-only policy during the hibernate-only post phase so userspace resumes with detached topology, without changing ordinary suspend or lid suspend behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Shutdown-mode hibernation powers off and restores the same boot/session; the hibernate-only post hook reconciles NVIDIA to detached/settled before user.slice thaws; direct hibernate and the final suspend-then-hibernate stage are covered; ordinary suspend does not invoke reconciliation; failures retain diagnostic evidence and controlled recovery; no forced shutdown is required.
notes:
Read-only ACPI analysis identifies the platform-S4 trigger. DSDT GPP0._PRW advertises GPE 0x08 for S4 wake when WKPM=1, matching enabled /proc/acpi/wakeup node pci:0000:00:01.1. Global _PTS handles Arg0=4 by calling DGHP(One). DGHP sets dGPU-present state, invokes GPP0.PG00._ON, waits 100ms, and notifies PEGP with a bus check. PG00._ON performs physical dGPU power-on and waits for NVIDIA vendor 0x10de. Linux acpi_hibernation_ops.pre_snapshot executes this ACPI preparation before create_image() checks pm_wakeup_pending(). Both failures then log GPP0 Card present, Link Up, and spurious PME with no competing S4 wake-device event. The exact wakeup-source object/IRQ was not printed because pm_debug_messages=0, but firmware-induced GPP0 hotplug is established as the rollback trigger. First workaround candidate: systemd HibernateMode=shutdown, which bypasses platform pre-snapshot callbacks and _PTS(4); unvalidated. Do not disable GPP0 wake first because firmware would still power on the dGPU during frozen topology. Do not retry platform mode. Any shutdown-mode test must first enable pm_debug_messages and pm_print_times and prepare immediate root capture of wakeup_sources, pm_wakeup_irq, graphics topology, and journal if it returns.
Prepared a fail-closed shutdown-mode validation path on 2026-09-02; activation and hardware testing remain pending. NixOS now sets the sole systemd HibernateMode value to shutdown and installs a direct-hibernate-only system-sleep evidence hook. systemd 261.2 replaces the parsed mode list on assignment, writes the configured mode before pre hooks, and aborts before /sys/power/state if that write fails, so there is no platform fallback. The guarded TTY runner enables and verifies pm_debug_messages/pm_print_times, starts a fresh persistent capture, quiesces graphical/audio clients, repeats authoritative root topology/client checks, explicitly selects and verifies [shutdown], and requires HIBERNATE-SHUTDOWN confirmation. Frozen pre/post evidence includes wakeup_sources, pm_wakeup_irq, PCI/graphics state, suspend counters, processes, failed units, and journals. The desktop is restarted only after detached/settled return; otherwise it remains stopped for Hybrid recovery. Bash/shfmt/ShellCheck, Nix formatting/evaluation, and a full host build pass. No lid or ordinary suspend setting was changed. sudo activation is blocked on an interactive password; do not treat this as a completed hibernate test.
SHUTDOWN-MODE TEST FAILED on 2026-09-02 in boot 76d2cb91 (request 12:40:25, return 12:42:17). Frozen pre-hook evidence proves /sys/power/disk=platform [shutdown] reboot suspend test_resume, so platform_pre_snapshot(false) bypassed ACPI _PTS(4). The kernel preallocated 12,595,068 KiB, froze devices, disabled CPUs, and entered create_image(), but never reached the 'Writing hibernation image' / swsusp_write path. With no dpm_suspend_end/syscore error logged, this is consistent with the remaining pm_wakeup_pending() branch before in_suspend=1. Wakeup-source counters did not change; 0000:00:01.1 remained zero. pm_wakeup_irq read 7 before kernel entry and no data afterward, so IRQ 7 is not yet attributable. GPP0 Card present/Link Up and NVIDIA enumeration occurred after CPUs/IRQs were restored, making dGPU hotplug a rollback consequence in shutdown mode rather than its trigger. mt7921e 0000:03:00.0 restore timed out with -110 afterward and last_failed_dev records it, but dpm_resume happens after create_image returns and does not cause the pre-image branch. Harness defects: systemctl hibernate is asynchronous, so the runner restored pm_debug_messages/pm_print_times before entry; frozen hook graphics capture lacked bash in PATH. Corrected to systemctl --wait, added Bash, made CLI capture optional, and removed lspci/link reads because they runtime-resumed GPP0 to D0 and perturbed the baseline. No corrected retest is authorized. User manually powered off at 12:49:11; current boot eb9dea5f reconciled detached/settled with zero failed units. Evidence: /var/log/legion-hibernate-diagnostics/2026-09-02T12-40-01+01-00-76d2cb91. Do not retry platform or shutdown mode while iGPU-only is selected.
Correction to the preceding harness note: systemctl --wait is not used and does not synchronize logind's asynchronous hibernate request. The final runner requires systemd-hibernate.service to be inactive before queuing, observes a changed nonzero ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic value, bounds and validates all systemctl property queries, then waits for inactive Result=success before restoring PM diagnostics. It treats missing required evidence, CAPTURE-FAILED, root graphics CLI failure, incomplete client inspection, nonempty clients, or non-detached/non-settled topology as fatal and keeps the graphical session stopped. Frozen captures now avoid the CLI, lspci, broad PCI scans, power_state, and link attributes; they use fixed-device presence, driver symlinks, and limited runtime power/wake reads. Final formatting, Bash syntax, ShellCheck, diff checks, side-effect review, and full NixOS host build pass. The corrected source has not been activated or hardware-retested. Investigation is blocked because the exact pm_wakeup_pending source requires another corrected hardware attempt, which is not authorized.
CORRECTION: the earlier pm_wakeup_pending/no-image conclusion was wrong. The preserved trace reached swsusp_save after the wakeup check, systemd observed a successful state write, and the wall/monotonic gap proves a powered-off interval followed by same-image restore. IRQ 7 was a stale AMD GPIO parent record and not the cause. The targeted fix adds reconcileGraphicsAfterHibernate, keyed to SYSTEMD_SLEEP_ACTION=hibernate during the post phase, with bounded udev settling, immutable PATH, and a 40-second hardened CLI reconciliation before user.slice thaw. Nix formatting/parsing, option evaluation, no-op dispatch checks, and a full local-input host build pass; deployment and controlled validation remain pending.
DEPLOYED VALIDATION on 2026-09-03 in boot fafd892b succeeded in restoring the shutdown-mode hibernation image; the kernel logged Hibernation image restored successfully. The one-shot post hook ran about 180 ms after hibernation exit and safely failed with effective=partial, inspection_complete=false, reconciliation=blocked, attempts=0. NVIDIA completed attached DRM/audio initialization roughly 1.3 seconds later, proving udevadm settle did not establish topology readiness. user.slice thawed and the guarded runner kept display-manager stopped; the system remained running with zero failed units. The revision retries authoritative root reconciliation every 2 seconds under a 60-second deadline, rejects clients and invalid/schema-unknown JSON immediately, and accepts only complete zero-client settled expected/effective topology. Focused shell tests, ShellCheck, Nix formatting, generated no-op dispatch checks, and a full local-input host build pass. Deployment and controlled resume validation remain pending.

Installed post hook invokes the validated retry loop under a 60-second timeout. Suspend-post and hibernate-pre no-op dispatch checks pass. Effective sleep config remains HibernateMode=shutdown. Graphics recovered detached/settled, display-manager is active, system state is running with zero failed units. GRUB generation limit 10 is deployed after cleaning /boot from 100% to 43%. Controlled hibernate resume validation remains pending.
VALIDATED SUCCESS on 2026-09-03 in boot fe05b2d8. Shutdown-mode hibernation powered off and restored the same image. Post hook observed partial/incomplete/blocked attempts=0 at monotonic 466.586, retried while NVIDIA initialized, then reported detached/settled, inspection_complete=true, active_clients=[], attempts=6 at 493.858. user.slice thawed at 493.862, after the authoritative result. title: Validate hibernate in iGPU-only mode
description: Validate hibernate and resume while generation 465 is settled in hybrid-igpu-only. Capture boot ID, graphics status, PCI/DRM topology, root-port power state, session state, failed units, and relevant kernel journal before hibernation and after resume. Treat a cold boot instead of resume as a failed validation and preserve safe recovery.
acceptance_criteria: The machine writes a hibernation image, powers down, resumes the same boot/session, retains selected hybrid-igpu-only policy with detached and settled NVIDIA topology, keeps the internal eDP panel functional, has no new failed units or NVIDIA/Legion kernel errors, and records evidence sufficient to distinguish resume from cold boot.
notes:
Preflight on 2026-09-02: login1 CanHibernate=yes; /sys/power/state includes disk and /sys/power/disk selected platform; 32 GiB swapfile active and unused for 32 GiB RAM; Plasma Wayland on eDP-2; selected/expected/effective hybrid-igpu-only/detached/detached and settled; NVIDIA PCI functions absent; root port 0000:00:01.1 runtime-suspended in D3cold; zero failed units. FAILED twice in boots 1b5154c8 and bc895c16. Both rolled back during S4 snapshot preparation before image creation or final platform power-down, immediately re-enumerated NVIDIA VGA/audio, and returned after 12.647s and 9.786s. The second attempt captured KWin DRM-lessee/output/EGL/card0 failures before the display became unusable. title: Fix legion WMI notify lifetime guard
description: The legion_wmi_notify callback reads legion_shared under legion_shared_mutex but uses if ((!priv) && (priv->loaded)), which dereferences priv when NULL and does not reject priv->loaded == false. After the unlock path it sleeps and calls legion_platform_profile_notify(priv->ppdev), so a late WMI event during probe/remove can dereference stale or NULL shared state. Fix callback lifetime handling without holding the shared mutex across the 500ms delay, and determine whether the unconditional delayed profile notification is still required.
acceptance_criteria: The callback returns safely when shared state is absent or unloading; no priv dereference occurs after its protected lifetime ends; WMI unregister/remove ordering prevents a concurrent stale callback; focused build/static checks pass; behavior is validated with event/remove race coverage where feasible.
close_reason: Fixed callback lifetime guard; revalidates shared state after delay and kernel 7.2.2 build/checkpatch pass.

title: Validate and deploy iGPU-only graphics modes
description: Deploy LenovoLegionLinux main c539a8637eb8f39a0aafe69241f921d6cc116e13 (graphics port 13dd1bf) on the Legion Slim 7 16APH8, perform the controlled Hybrid to Hybrid iGPU-only and Auto hardware matrix, prove BIOS rollback, then enable the firmware-advertised modes in the Flutter frontend.
acceptance_criteria: Hardened driver and combined graphics-mode CLI are deployed; Hybrid iGPU-only and Auto are validated across PCI/DRM topology, internal and external displays, Wayland session survival, suspend/resume, AC/battery transitions, reboot persistence, and BIOS rollback; Flutter consumes status/choices and enables only advertised modes with tests.
notes:
The original graphics commit 5a2a2d1 was ported onto current upstream as 13dd1bf and is included in fork main c539a86. Python tests, CLI smoke test, checkpatch, kernel module build, and full NixOS toplevel build passed; disruptive hardware validation remains pending reboot.
2026-08-31 live Hybrid -> Hybrid iGPU-only attempt: firmware readback changed to gsync=1/igpumode=1, but stopping display-manager.service left the existing Plasma Wayland session alive. Firmware unbound NVIDIA DRM while kwin_wayland still held the GPU; kernel logged 'NVRM: Attempting to remove device 0000:01:00.0 with non-zero usage count!'. The VGA function remained present and unbound, NVIDIA audio disappeared, nvidia-smi reported no device, and live Hybrid rollback restored firmware readback but did not rebind PCI drivers. Reboot recovered clean Hybrid state with both NVIDIA functions bound. Revised procedure must terminate the graphical login session with SIGKILL and verify KWin/Plasma/Xwayland absence before retrying.
Second clean-TTY attempt stopped graphical-session.target successfully (no KWin, Plasma, or Xwayland), but firmware ejection again logged non-zero NVIDIA usage. lsof identified the remaining holder exactly: VS Code PID 2903 retained /dev/nvidiactl after the graphical target stopped. Resulting topology: igpumode=1, AMD-only DRM, NVIDIA audio function absent, NVIDIA VGA function present but unbound. Safety gate must inspect actual /dev/nvidia* open handles; stopping Plasma/logout alone is insufficient because detached Electron/Code processes can survive.
Reboot persistence result: selector persisted as gsync=1/igpumode=1 and Plasma/internal AMD panel booted, but NVIDIA did not remain ejected. NVIDIA VGA/audio enumerated and bound before legion_laptop loaded; nvidia-drm/card1 loaded and KWin reopened the dGPU. Therefore igpumode is a selected policy, not proof of effective topology. Linux requires Lenovo's NotifyDGPUStatus reconciliation (Windows LLT retries every 5s up to 5 times when iGPU-only is selected and dGPU remains available), plus an active-client safety gate/early-boot orchestration. Current combined status is insufficient if it reports selector only.
Backend safety/effective-state contract implemented and pushed as LenovoLegionLinux 78f33ee. Adds structured selected/effective/expected status, root /proc fd scanning for NVIDIA and associated DRM handles, fail-closed Auto power/topology inspection, immediate pre-write recheck, observed-state NotifyDGPUStatus reconciliation (5 attempts x 5 seconds), truthful blocked/pending exit codes, and CI unit discovery. 28 focused tests pass; Nix lenovo-legion app and kernel module builds pass. Live negative test identified Xwayland and Code and exited 2 while selector remained Hybrid. Full NixOS switch deferred because the dotfiles worktree has unrelated active flake/kernel/hardware/RGB changes; next clean transition can use built CLI /nix/store/6wf7b61b1np3hm7rv53vsmzsb035qpd7-lenovo-legion-app-0.0.22-unstable-2026-08-21/bin/legion_cli.
Successful guarded live transition at 2026-08-31 12:37: root preflight reported zero dGPU clients with complete inspection; Hybrid -> Hybrid iGPU-only converged in 2 reconciliation attempts. Selected=hybrid-igpu-only, expected/effective=detached, exit=0. NVIDIA VGA/audio PCI functions and card1 DRM disappeared; only AMD card2/eDP-2 remained, and Plasma/Wayland restarted successfully on the internal panel. Kernel logged normal NVIDIA DRM remove/unload and no NVRM non-zero usage warning. Root port logged 'Refused to change power state from D0 to D3hot', but topology remained detached and functional. Evidence: /tmp/lllf-igpu-only-2026-08-31T12-37-01+01-00.log.
iGPU-only suspend/resume passed: s2idle entered 12:39:55 and exited 12:40:02; internal AMD eDP resumed, legion_laptop resumed, selector remained gsync=1/igpumode=1, effective NVIDIA topology remained detached, and Plasma stayed functional. No NVIDIA re-enumeration or dGPU error occurred. Residual: repeated 'pcieport 0000:00:08.1: PME: Spurious native interrupt!' after resume concerns the AMD/iGPU root port, not the detached NVIDIA 00:01.1 path; track separately if it persists outside graphics testing.
Successful guarded live rollback at 2026-08-31 14:59: Hybrid iGPU-only -> Hybrid converged in 1 reconciliation attempt with complete root client inspection and exit 0. NVIDIA VGA 01:00.0 and audio 01:00.1 hot-added; nvidia and snd_hda_intel rebound, NVIDIA DRM card0/renderD128 appeared, nvidia-smi succeeded, and Plasma restarted with KWin using the dGPU. Selected=hybrid, expected/effective=attached, reconciliation=settled. No non-zero usage-count or partial-rebind failure. Residual post-bind messages: known SBIOS target-temperature/platform-power assertions, duplicate ACPI video warning, and DP-2 EDID warning. Evidence: /tmp/lllf-restore-hybrid-2026-08-31T14-58-56+01-00.log.
Successful guarded Hybrid -> Hybrid Auto transition on AC at 2026-08-31 15:20: Hybrid Auto selected with ACAD=1; expected/effective dGPU state remained attached and settled in 1 reconciliation attempt with complete root client inspection and exit 0. NVIDIA VGA/audio remained driver-bound, NVIDIA DRM remained present, nvidia-smi succeeded, and Plasma restarted on the internal panel. No PCI hotplug or dGPU failure occurred. Residual 00:08.1 PME warning continued. Evidence: /tmp/lllf-auto-ac-2026-08-31T15-20-41+01-00.log.
Successful guarded Hybrid Auto AC -> battery transition at 2026-08-31 17:17. Root preflight was complete with zero clients and attached/settled Auto on AC. After ACAD changed to 0, expected state became detached but effective state remained attached for observations 0-27, became partial at observation 28, and settled detached at observation 29 (about 29 seconds) without explicit backend reconciliation. NVIDIA PCI and DRM disappeared; Plasma restarted on AMD/internal eDP; selected=hybrid-auto, expected/effective=detached, exit=0. No NVRM non-zero usage warning. Residual teardown messages: NVIDIA HDMI audio 'probed, but not operational' and 00:01.1 D0->D3hot refusal; repeated 00:08.1 PME warning continues. Evidence: /tmp/lllf-auto-battery-2026-08-31T17-17-01+01-00.log.
Hybrid Auto battery suspend/resume passed at 2026-08-31 17:21-17:23: s2idle resumed through AMD and legion_laptop, pciehp explicitly reported NVIDIA slot 00:01.1 absent, AC remained offline, and selected=hybrid-auto with expected/effective=detached and reconciliation=settled. Plasma/internal eDP remained functional; no NVIDIA re-enumeration or dGPU error. Residual 00:08.1 PME warning continued.
Hybrid Auto battery -> AC native reattach passed at 2026-08-31 17:25:48 with Plasma running. ACAD=1 caused PCI hot-add of NVIDIA VGA/audio; nvidia and snd_hda_intel bound, NVIDIA DRM returned, nvidia-smi succeeded, and selected=hybrid-auto with expected/effective=attached and reconciliation=settled. Known duplicate ACPI video, SBIOS target-temp/platform-power assertions, DP-2 EDID warning, and 00:08.1 PME warning recurred; no bind failure. Safety finding: Auto cannot remain selected for normal use or be frontend-enabled yet because a later AC unplug triggers firmware ejection independently of the CLI active-client guard and may occur while Plasma/Xwayland holds NVIDIA.
Final safe-state restore completed at 2026-08-31 17:29: Hybrid Auto -> plain Hybrid settled in 1 attempt with complete root inspection and zero clients. AC is online; NVIDIA VGA/audio remain attached and driver-bound; NVIDIA DRM, nvidia-smi, Plasma, and internal eDP are healthy. Current selected=hybrid, expected/effective=attached. Evidence: /tmp/lllf-restore-hybrid-2026-08-31T17-29-36+01-00.log.
Post-validation scope split: lllf-j9t.1 tracks early-boot reconciliation before display-manager; lllf-j9t.2 tracks read-only authoritative combined graphics status and removal of misleading binary UI; lllf-j9t.3 tracks a later typed controlled iGPU-only privileged workflow and depends on lllf-j9t.1. Hybrid Auto remains intentionally non-actionable because autonomous AC-loss ejection cannot be made race-free by userspace monitoring.
Frontend integration now includes early-boot reconciliation, strict authoritative combined status, and guarded non-Auto typed controls. TTY validation helpers use the immutable current-system CLI path and fail-safe display-manager cleanup. Full hardware deployment/reboot and remaining external-display/X11/hibernate/cold-boot/BIOS checks remain open.
2026-09-01 generation-464 live Flutter validation closed lllf-j9t.3: with Code/Xwayland holding dGPU/DRM devices and root inspection incomplete, the confirmed Hybrid iGPU-only request authorized through persistent LegionControl1 and returned typed GraphicsBlocked. UI recovery guidance was accurate; authoritative readback remained settled Hybrid with attached expected/effective topology and zero failed units. Native Nix package/CTest, 69 focused Flutter tests, analyzer, and Linux debug build passed.

title: Harden fan control: EC settle/readback and fan role labels
description:
LLT v2.38 found that a single immediate readback after an EC write can be wrong. Its fan-table path waits for the EC, reads twice with a delay, retries up to three times, and reports failure without discarding the user's curve (GodModeController.SetFanTableWithVerifyAsync; commits 283ce6f6, af9bd0f1, bf8ba3d1, 4a72f584). Our FansBloc already preserves drafts and compares readback.

Work:
- Determine whether legion_cli/sysfs needs a bounded settle delay and double read before we call a fan write stale. Test on the laptop; do not copy the Windows 500 ms delay blindly.
- If the CLI needs a readback or retry contract, open a scoped upstream/CLI issue or PR and keep the frontend truthful about partial or unconfirmed writes.
- Keep the current behavior of preserving the draft and reporting the mismatch; never auto-replace the requested curve with the current EC table.
- Fan identity: LLT's FanTableTypeResolver maps fan/sensor IDs to CPU, GPUSensor, GPU2, and SystemFan. Our FanChannel enum and labels assume fan 1 is CPU and fan 2 is GPU (lib/features/fans/view/fan_curve_editor.dart and fans_page.dart). Before enabling level-table editing, derive the role from the driver/capabilities or use neutral Fan 1/Fan 2 labels where the role is unknown. Do not label a system fan as CPU or GPU.

Related: lllf-6p0, lllf-em2, lllf-l5i, lllf-vac.
acceptance_criteria: Hardware evidence establishes whether a settle/double-read policy is needed. The chosen retry policy is bounded, preserves drafts, and reports stale, transient, clamped, and failed writes truthfully. If the CLI needs work, an issue or PR is linked. Fan labels are capability-driven or neutral where the role is unknown, with tests for shared and system-fan tables.

title: Decide persistent OSD scope and platform-surface lifecycle
description:
LLT v2.38 now has a persistent, customizable sensor OSD: panel and bar styles, item selection, warning/critical thresholds, colors, font size, opacity, corner radius, click-through lock, monitor-relative position, and session-lock hiding. It repositions after display and DPI changes and subscribes to sensor updates only while visible (LenovoLegionToolkit.WPF/Windows/Osd/OsdWindowBase.cs).

Our planned OSD in lllf-cqn.7.1 is a transient event popup, not a persistent sensor monitor. We need a product decision before building further:
- Keep the transient event OSD only.
- Add a persistent sensor OSD later, reusing the existing Dashboard/Analytics data.
- Stage both, with the transient popup first.

Regardless of that decision, the platform-surface lifecycle needs:
- Hide the OSD and suppress notifications while the session is locked.
- Reposition on display, resolution, and DPI changes.
- Save positions relative to a monitor and clamp into its work area.
- Subscribe to sensors only while a surface is visible; use one shared sampler rather than adding another timer beside the dashboard, battery, and live-sensor pollers.
- Tray and window: preserve maximized state when hiding and restoring, restore into the monitor that contained the saved rectangle, and activate the existing instance on a second launch.

Related work: lllf-cqn.7.1, lllf-cqn.7.2, lllf-wc5, lllf-b7x, lllf-qei.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded for transient-only versus persistent sensor OSD. Follow-up issues carry the session-lock, display/DPI, monitor-relative position, visible-surface sampling, maximized-state, and single-instance requirements. No additional polling or surface code starts before that decision.

title: Open the existing app window when launched again
description:
The app can start in the tray and keep running when its window closes. It currently creates the application with `G_APPLICATION_NON_UNIQUE`, so a second launch starts another process. The second process contends for Hive storage locks and can show the startup failure tracked in `lllf-wzb`. Users will click the app icon to reopen a hidden window, so a second launch must activate the existing instance instead.

## Desired behavior

- A manual launch while the app is running shows and focuses the existing window.
- The second launch does not start another Flutter engine, open Hive boxes again, or delete lock files.
- If the existing instance does not respond, allow a clean new launch or report a specific failure. Do not silently claim success.
- Start-in-tray, close-to-tray, and the tray menu continue to work.

## Investigation

- Use GApplication's single-instance activation by removing `G_APPLICATION_NON_UNIQUE` and tracking the main window in `my_application_activate`, or use a session-bus name with an activate call. Choose the simpler supported path.
- Preserve `g_set_prgname(APPLICATION_ID)` so the desktop maps the running app to its `.desktop` file.
- Check the installed package and the AppImage.
- Do not work around the Hive lock by deleting files or bypassing exclusive access.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A manual launch while the login instance is hidden shows the existing window and focuses it.
- Only one process owns the Hive storage.
- No lock files are deleted.
- A stale or unresponsive instance does not block a clean recovery. The app reports the failure and gives a recovery step.
- Tests cover second-launch activation, no duplicate engine or Hive open, and the unresponsive-instance path.
- A desktop check records the behavior for the installed app and the AppImage on KDE Wayland.
- Docs describe the single-instance behavior and the recovery path.

title: Start the app at login in the tray and support close-to-tray, including from an AppImage
description:
The app has no login-start option, and the tray is implemented but not connected. Keyboard automation and idle lighting only work while the app runs. The installed app should start at login in the tray, and closing the window should return it to the tray. The AppImage should do the same when the host provides a StatusNotifier host.

## Desired behavior

- Add a `Start at login` switch to Settings. The default is off.
- Enabling it writes a standard XDG autostart entry at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/io.github.prnice.legion_linux_frontend.desktop`, defaulting to `~/.config/autostart/io.github.prnice.legion_linux_frontend.desktop`. Disabling it removes only that file.
- The autostart entry passes `--start-hidden` to the app.
- On a login launch with `--start-hidden`, start in the tray without showing the main window. Do not show the window first and then hide it.
- A manual launch without `--start-hidden` shows the window normally.
- Closing the main window hides it to the tray and keeps the app running. This is close-to-tray.
- The minimize button continues to minimize the window normally. Do not route minimize through the tray.
- If no tray host is available, ignore `--start-hidden` and show the window. The app must never start hidden without a reachable tray.
- If the tray disappears while the window is hidden, show the window so the app remains reachable.
- Session logout and shutdown exit the app normally. Close-to-tray must not keep the app alive across logout or block shutdown.
- The tray menu has `Open` (show and focus) and `Quit` (exit through the normal shutdown path). Quit must bypass close-to-tray.

## Tray integration

The tray connection is tracked in `lllf-cqn.7.2`. This issue consumes it and adds start-in-tray and close-to-tray.

- Connect one `PlatformTray(DBusTrayTransport())` for the app lifetime.
- Install a `YaruWindow.onClose` handler. When the tray is usable, hide the window and return `false` to cancel the close. Otherwise allow the close.
- Use `YaruWindow.ensureInitialized()` and its `hide()`/`show()` methods. Keep the app running while hidden.
- The native runner currently shows the window on the first Flutter frame. Make it honor `--start-hidden` so the window stays hidden until Dart decides whether the tray is usable.
- `PlatformTray` currently treats watcher registration as success. Extend it to check `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher.IsStatusNotifierHostRegistered` before treating the tray as usable for hidden startup or close-to-tray. Registration alone does not prove a host displays the icon.
- If the watcher or host is absent, start with the window visible and close normally. Settings explains why the tray behavior is unavailable.
- If the tray changes state while hidden, show the window on loss.
- Do not add hardware actions to the tray; the existing confirmation and privileged flow stays unchanged.

## Launch path

- For an AppImage, the entry starts the AppImage file itself. Read the absolute path from the `APPIMAGE` environment variable that the AppImage runtime sets. Do not use `Platform.resolvedExecutable`, which points into the temporary extraction directory.
- For the native package, start the installed `legion_frontend` command. On NixOS, do not write the current `/nix/store/...` path because it changes on upgrade.
- Quote and escape the path for the Desktop Entry `Exec` key. Paths with spaces, quotes, backslashes, and `%` must work. Set `TryExec` to the same launch path and `X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true`.
- If the AppImage moves after the user enables the setting, update the entry on the next launch. If the app cannot determine a stable launch path, disable the switch and explain why.
- Autostart makes a second manual launch more likely. A manual launch while the login instance is hidden should open the existing window; that behavior is tracked in `lllf-b7x`. Do not bypass the storage lock in the meantime. If the existing lock behavior prevents a clean second launch, record the limitation and link `lllf-wzb`.

## AppImage tray

- The tray uses the session D-Bus and does not depend on installation. The AppImage should register the same StatusNotifierItem on a host with a watcher and host.
- Verify the AppImage on KDE Wayland: start at login in the tray, close the window to the tray, open from the tray, and quit from the tray.
- If the AppImage cannot register or display the tray for a packaging-specific reason, record the exact failure and start with the window visible. Do not add a custom tray helper or launcher.
- Use the standard `computer` icon or the packaged app icon through `IconPixmap`. The host may not see the AppImage's private icon directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Settings switch persists across restarts.
- Enabling it creates a valid autostart file that starts the app after the next desktop login on KDE Wayland.
- On the installed app, login starts in the tray with no visible window and no window flash. The tray icon opens the window and quits the app.
- Closing the window hides it to the tray and keeps the app running.
- The minimize button still minimizes the window to the taskbar or panel; it does not hide to the tray.
- If no StatusNotifier host is registered, login shows the window and close exits the app. Settings explains why the tray behavior is unavailable.
- If the tray disappears while hidden, the window returns.
- Session logout and shutdown exit the app normally; close-to-tray does not block them.
- A manual launch shows the window normally.
- An AppImage stored in a path with spaces starts in the tray on KDE Wayland, closes to the tray, opens from the tray, and quits. If it cannot, the issue records the limitation and the window starts visible.
- The native Nix package starts from the autostart entry after a package upgrade without keeping an old store path.
- A moved AppImage updates the entry on the next launch, or the UI reports that it cannot.
- Quit from the tray exits the app through the normal shutdown path and does not just hide the window again.
- Tests cover enabling, disabling, path escaping, AppImage versus native path selection, hidden startup, close-to-tray, minimize remaining normal, tray host absence, tray loss while hidden, and Open/Quit menu actions.
- The tray menu has no hardware actions and the existing confirmation flow is unchanged.
- Docs and README describe the setting, start-in-tray, close-to-tray, minimize behavior, and the AppImage limits. Update `docs/platform-tray.md` and `docs/appimage.md`.

title: Apply the assigned keyboard profile when the app starts
description:
The app stores a keyboard profile for each power mode and applies an assignment when its automation config and the dashboard power mode are available. The native restart journey covers that happy path in a new process. The remaining risk is startup ordering: the shell needs the config, the current power mode, and a ready keyboard backend. If any of them arrives late, the assignment can be missed and the app keeps the last saved manual lighting.

## Desired behavior

- On every app launch, including a launch at login, apply the profile assigned to the current power mode without requiring the user to open Lighting or Automation.
- If the current power mode is not known yet, wait for it and apply the assignment once it is known.
- If the keyboard backend is not ready yet, wait for it and retry the assignment when it becomes available. Do not show a failure dialog for a backend that is still starting.
- If the current mode has no assignment, restore the last saved lighting snapshot as the app does today. Do not apply another mode's profile.
- If the saved profile is missing or does not fit the keyboard, show the existing retryable error and keep the previous lighting. Do not fall back silently.
- A manual edit made after launch stays in place until the next assigned mode change or explicit profile application, as it does today.

## Investigation

- Reproduce a cold app launch with an assigned profile and no page navigation. Check the order of `RgbLightingStarted`, `AutomationStarted`, the first dashboard power-profile reading, and `RgbProfileLoaded`.
- Check a launch where the native Spectrum or OpenRGB backend becomes available after the first lighting load.
- Check a launch where the dashboard cannot read the power mode. Decide whether to keep waiting, apply the last saved snapshot, or explain why no assignment applied.
- Keep the existing write queue so startup, manual edits, and mode changes do not interleave.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh process with an assigned profile applies that profile before the user opens Lighting or Automation.
- A fresh process with no assignment restores the last saved snapshot and does not apply another mode's profile.
- Delayed power-mode and delayed keyboard-backend cases apply the assignment once both are ready, without a false error dialog.
- A missing or incompatible profile shows the existing retryable failure and leaves the previous lighting in place.
- The app does not apply the same assignment repeatedly when unrelated telemetry or navigation changes.
- Tests cover cold startup with an assignment, no assignment, delayed power mode, delayed backend, missing profile, and incompatible profile.
- The native restart journey continues to prove that the assigned profile overrides a different manual snapshot in a new process.
- `docs/keyboard-automation.md` states when the profile applies and what happens when startup data is delayed.

title: Turn keyboard lighting off after idle and restore it on activity
description:
MacBooks turn the keyboard backlight off after a short idle period and turn it back on at the next key press or trackpad touch. This app leaves keyboard lighting on while it runs.

## Desired behavior

- Add a `Turn off when idle` switch and a timeout choice. Suggested choices: 30 seconds, 1 minute, 2 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, and Never.
- After the whole desktop session stays idle for the chosen time, turn the keyboard lighting off.
- The next keyboard or pointer input restores the lighting that was visible before the timeout. A named profile, manual painting, brightness, and software effect return exactly as they were.
- The idle state must not overwrite the saved lighting snapshot or named profiles.
- If the app exits while the lighting is off, it restores the saved lighting before closing so the keyboard is not left dark.
- Support both native Spectrum and OpenRGB backends. If neither backend can turn the lighting off, disable the control and explain why.

## Idle detection

Wayland blocks global input monitoring, so the app cannot read key events directly. Use the session idle time from `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime` on the session bus. KDE and GNOME provide this interface. Poll at a low rate while the feature is enabled.

Investigate a fallback through `org.freedesktop.login1.Session.IdleHint` for desktops without a screen saver service. If no supported idle source exists, disable the setting and explain why. Do not add privileged input access.

Check whether brightness 0 turns each backend off. If it does not, write a black Direct frame and restore the previous mode afterwards.

## Where it lives

- Add the controls to Lighting or a Settings section. Follow `docs/page-template.md` and `docs/error-and-feedback-standard.md`.
- Persist the enabled flag and timeout in the existing `preferences` Hive box. Default to off so the app does not change lighting without the user's choice.
- Document the behavior, supported desktops, and the app-must-run limit in `docs/keyboard-automation.md` or a new lighting document. Update the README feature table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Enabling the timeout turns the keyboard lighting off after the chosen idle period and restores the exact previous state on the next input.
- Disabling the setting, or choosing Never, leaves the lighting unchanged.
- The saved snapshot, named profiles, and brightness stay unchanged across an idle off/on cycle and an app restart.
- Closing the app while the lighting is off restores the saved lighting before the process exits.
- The UI reports an unavailable idle source or unsupported backend instead of silently doing nothing.
- Unit tests cover timeout, activity, disabled, unavailable, profile-change-while-idle, and close-while-idle paths with a fake idle source and fake lighting backend.
- A native app journey covers the setting and an idle off/on cycle with the fake idle source.
- Hardware checks on the test device record whether brightness 0 turns off the native Spectrum and OpenRGB backlights and whether the restore works. Record the desktop and session type.
- Docs and README describe the feature and its limits.

title: Qualify frontend compatibility and UI after the M1CN backend upgrade
description:
# Upgrade follow-up checklist

## Scope and evidence

Compare old fork `dec598335b9482c4b63ff02f34c1bc26d1d6cabc`, upstream
`98531565555d43c2e34c2c487ffcbba273c5e803`, and merged fork
`baafe12ccb4bea628aecccfb0e53309fa9c6be00`.
Hardware: Lenovo 82Y4, Legion Slim 7 16APH8, BIOS M1CN48WW.
Frontend source inspected at `7a212f28764c39fa5b23fe60e5da1bc3b365e8e5`.
Line numbers below refer to that snapshot; use the named functions after files move.

This is a source-based compatibility review, not a visual audit or hardware
qualification. No frontend implementation, module activation, GPU transition,
power write, or unvalidated fan write is approved by this checklist.

Driver PR: https://github.com/Prn-Ice/LenovoLegionLinux/pull/3.
System pin PR: https://github.com/Prn-Ice/nixos-flaky-tests/pull/2.
The backend passed 161 tests, its M1CN C store harness, the 505-case fan
capability fixture, lint, Nix package/module builds, and all seven hosted
checks. The local full system build passed without activation. None of that
establishes the new module's hardware behavior.

## 1. Fans: supported controls, units, and write eligibility

Owner: existing `lllf-cqn.8`; lock guidance: `lllf-nnd`.

Upstream `5deb227` marks M1CN as level-index, speed-only, with no valid legacy
minifancurve or controller-lock registers. Fan-table writes are unvalidated
and rejected by default. Do not bypass that guard to make the frontend work.

### UI changes to check

| Section / element | Disposition on M1CN | Source to inspect/change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fans -> Reduce fan cycling (`mini-fan-curve`) | Hide when unsupported. The existing null-based conditional already hides it when the new driver removes the attribute; verify this rather than delete the shared widget. | `lib/features/fans/view/fans_page.dart::_FanControls` (~355-366); `lib/core/services/legion_sysfs_service.dart::readMiniFanCurveMode`; `lib/features/fans/repository/fans_repository.dart::loadSnapshot` |
| Fans -> Lock fan controller (`lock-fan-controller`) | Hide on M1CN. Do not offer an enable/disable action for the old EC byte. Keep support on models with a validated register. | `fans_page.dart::_FanControls` (~378-388), `_setLockFanController` (~170-183); `readLockFanControllerMode`; `lllf-nnd` |
| Fans -> preset chips | Do not offer active preset-write actions while fan writes are unsupported or unvalidated. The toolbar currently enables chips based only on `!isApplying`, even when the curve is unavailable. Hide the write-only picker or disable it with the safety reason; do not prompt for authentication for a known-blocked action. | `fans_page.dart::_FanWorkspaceToolbar` (~245-257), `_applyPreset`; `FansRepository::defaultPresets`, `applyPreset`, `applyCurrentContextPreset`; `FansBloc` write handlers |
| Fans -> draggable curve and Apply curve | Keep read-only until the backend reports a supported, qualified write path. A readable curve does not prove write permission. Apply the guard in state/repository/action handling as well as the widget, including stale edits after capabilities disappear. | `fans_page.dart` (~70-92); `fan_curve_editor.dart::_canEdit`, `_SaveRow`; `fans_bloc.dart::_onFanCurvePointUpdated`, `_onFanCurveSaveRequested`, `_reloadState`; state/snapshot models |
| Fans -> Temperature axis, temperature slider, Hysteresis, Ramp | Hide unsupported editable fields for a speed-only table. Delete invented fallback temperatures/ramps from the M1CN display path, not valid controls for other models. If there is trustworthy read-only table data, use point/level coordinates rather than an invented temperature curve. | `lib/features/fans/view/fan_curve_editor.dart::_temperature`, `_spots`, `_buildChart`, `_buildSummaryCards`, `_buildPointControls` (~164-680) |
| Fans -> Fan speed % / RPM mapping | Do not present arbitrary percentages or a guessed linear RPM conversion as firmware levels. Use the driver's reported unit and firmware RPM ladders when available; otherwise show levels or unavailable RPM. Never fill missing ladders from another laptop. | `fan_curve_editor.dart::_maxRpm`, `_rpm`, `_boundedRpm`, `_updateFromPosition`; `lib/features/fans/models/fan_curve.dart` |
| Fans -> CPU/GPU curve selector | Do not imply two independently writable curves when WMI exposes one speed table. Adapt the curve selector only after identifying the real model contract. Keep both real live fan-RPM and temperature readouts; do not delete telemetry because editing is blocked. Verify fan-to-CPU/GPU naming separately. | `fans_page.dart::FanChannel` use / `_FanWorkspaceToolbar`; `fan_curve_editor.dart::FanChannel`, `FanCurveUnavailablePanel` |
| Fans -> Maximum fan speed | Do not remove merely because curve writes are blocked. It uses a separate firmware operation. Verify support, safe behavior, and readback independently, then keep or hide based on the result. | `fans_page.dart::_setMaximumFanSpeed`, `_FanControls`; `readMaximumFanSpeedMode`; `lllf-5kk` |

### Data and state changes to check

- `lib/core/services/legion_sysfs_service.dart::readFanCurve` (~471 onward)
  currently requires two PWM files, CPU/GPU/IC temperature pairs, and
  acceleration/deceleration for ten points. That rejects the corrected WMI3
  speed-only schema. Read supported fields and point counts without inventing
  the missing ones.
- `lib/features/fans/models/fan_curve.dart` requires all legacy fields and
  defaults both maximum RPM values to 5000. Replace those assumptions with a
  capability-aware model; use enums for units/statuses. Do not silently turn
  a firmware initializer table into a claimed live hardware curve.
- Carry readable/writable/unvalidated/unsupported/permission-error distinctions
  through `fans_snapshot.dart`, `fans_state.dart`, `fans_repository.dart`, and
  `fans_bloc.dart`. Sysfs file presence or Unix mode bits alone do not establish
  that the driver's runtime safety guard allows a write.
- The model's old fan capture remains limited: a firmware table can contain
  initializer constants instead of the programmed live curve. Retain the
  evidence and uncertainty in `docs/architecture/m1cn-hardware-evidence.md`.

### Copy and diagnostics to check

- `fan_curve_editor.dart:123`: "could not read the temperature and fan-speed
  settings needed to edit a curve" conflates a legitimate speed-only schema,
  a safety block, and an I/O failure. Use cause-specific copy. For a confirmed
  unvalidated-write block, propose: "Fan-curve changes have not been validated
  for this laptop. Current fan speeds and temperatures remain available."
- `fans_page.dart:179`: "Disable it before returning fan control to another
  tool" has not been established as a cross-tool requirement. Hide the action
  on unsupported M1CN; verify semantics before retaining that warning elsewhere.
- `lib/core/models/hardware_check.dart` and About diagnostics should still
  report missing versus unreadable controls. Hiding an unsupported action must
  not erase diagnostic evidence or call a permission failure unsupported.
- Preserve the page-template rule: hide unsupported secondary controls; explain
  a blocked main feature in place and retain useful readings. Use the existing
  error/feedback standard, not new banners or force-enable guidance.

Acceptance: fixtures for old full-schema hardware, new M1CN speed-only hardware,
missing ladders, unsupported controls, permission failures, no curve, changing
capabilities, and stale dirty drafts. Verify no callback or privileged dispatch
for blocked curve/preset writes, no fake temperature/RPM data, supported-model
controls remain, and live telemetry survives. Extend the existing fan discovery,
model, Bloc, editor, and page tests under `test/core/services/` and
`test/features/fans/`.

## 2. Power: firmware bounds, partial defaults, and unsupported rows

Owners: `lllf-dok`, `lllf-zfg`, and `lllf-6p0`.

- `lib/features/power/repository/power_repository.dart::allPowerLimits`
  (~39-143) and `control/control_commands.cc::ints` (~15-24) use broad app

Owners: `lllf-6p0` and native journey follow-up `lllf-gcc.3`.

## 5. Seven local fixes: redundancy audit

| Local commit | Finding against upstream 9853156 | Disposition |

Revisit zero-based field visibility under `lllf-dok`: a zero read alone is not authoritative support/default evidence, especially for PPAB. |

Upstream also fixes the WMI event null/unloaded predicate, but still lacks the local early return plus post-delay lifetime/loaded recheck under the shared mutex. It also lacks the combined graphics CLI, checked selector transactions, rollback, and graphics support gating. | Keep the transaction and lifetime safeguards; do not drop this whole commit because the initial predicate overlaps. The fork's wildcard discovery also remains different from upstream's kernel-version paths. |

Upstream `wmi_exec_arg` still passes NULL for the return buffer; the fork allocates and frees it. | Retain pending a separately justified change. This patch does not parse the firmware result or establish hardware success; readback remains required. |
| `eb984e8` avoid unnecessary dmesg reads | Not superseded. Upstream still evaluates `get_dmesg()` eagerly in `LegionModelFacade` even when INFO logging is off. | Keep the local logging-level guard and captured stderr behavior. |
| `159e376` GPU temperature writes through WMI3 | Superseded. Upstream's `gpu_temperature_limit_store` now routes ACCESS_METHOD_WMI3 through `wmi_common_method_other_store` for `OtherMethodFeature_GPU_TEMPERATURE_LIMIT`. | Already de-duplicated during the merge: upstream's equivalent branch remains, the second local branch was removed. | `dec5983` dGPU detach lifecycle | Not superseded. Upstream lacks the local handling of every NVIDIA function, HDMI-audio device holders, and final-availability notifications. | Keep it with the graphics tests; do not weaken inspection to permit a transition. |

Do not rewrite fork history or revert an entire mixed-purpose commit as
"cleanup." Compare behavior and remove only a proven duplicate implementation.

AppRun only adds AppDir usr/share to child XDG_DATA_DIRS, not compositor paths. Plasma task manager also has APPDIR environment fallback, but that does not replace KWin window lookup. title: Resolve the empty initial cursor name in the Flutter Linux engine

comments.text:
# Copy and comment sweep coverage — 2026-11-11

Issue: lllf-dek. Inventory baseline: 29cbaf5 on cleanup/stashed-copy.
Reviewed first-party prose/comment extracts across every included file, with surrounding code and serializers checked for factual claims. Blank/non-prose files are included in counts, not treated as writing defects.
This pass preserves runtime behavior, commands, identifiers, evidence, warnings, quotations, and prior readability work. It is not a visual redesign or a hardware-support certification.

## Inventory rules

Start with git ls-files. Exclude symbolic links; .agent/, .agents/, .opencode/, .beads/, inspiration/, linux/flutter/; .g.dart, .png, .svg, .lock, .patch; LICENSE, skills-lock.json, .metadata; and binary files. Within included docs, preserve license/quotation bodies and historical evidence. Markdown belongs to docs; remaining lib/ to app; test/ and integration_test/ to tests; control/, telemetry/, linux/ to native; remaining text to tools/config.

- docs: 30 files reviewed.
- app: 196 files reviewed.
- native: 65 files reviewed.
- tests: 143 files reviewed.
- tools: 51 files reviewed.
- Total included: 485. Excluded: 231.

## Corrections and reasons

- lib/features/power/view/power_page.dart: "verified hardware defaults" asserted evidence we do not have. It now explains recorded model/BIOS references and labels both primary and additional values "Reference". Values, hardwareDefault identifiers, and keys stay unchanged. Related source comments and docs/model-support.md use the same distinction.
- lib/features/battery/view/battery_page.dart: "not exposed by the battery driver" guessed a cause from a missing value. Detail and history now say temperature is unavailable. The widget test selects the temperature series and checks that message.
- lib/features/dashboard/widgets/mode_hero.dart: "Quick when you need it, calm when you do not" was vague. "Balances performance and power use" names the trade-off.
- lib/features/fans/view/fan_curve_editor.dart: "Tachometer unavailable" used unnecessary jargon; "Fan speed unavailable" names the missing reading. "The hardware curve is up to date" claimed hardware freshness from editor dirty state; "No unsaved curve changes" reports only that state.
- lib/features/fans/view/fans_page.dart: "Exclusive fan control" / "Prevent other tools" promised cross-tool exclusion not established by frontend code. The control now uses the driver-named lock and neutral help text. The existing safety warning remains.
- lib/features/lighting/view/lighting_page.dart: "backlight toggles below remain available" promised unavailable controls. The message now says separate controls appear when supported. Device/backend and picker comments describe the current implementation without stale magenta/OpenRGB-only claims.
- lib/core/widgets/app_shell_components.dart: "protected preflight" and "GPU topology" obscured consequences. Messages now name safety checks and GPU configuration while preserving blocked-before-write versus accepted-but-unconfirmed distinctions. Tests assert those distinctions.
- lib/core/services/legion_sysfs_service.dart: the battery-cycle comment hard-coded BAT0 despite discovery; the CPU-policy comment assumed identical policy across domains; duplicate fan-curve comments obscured the monotonicity check. Each now states what the code actually reads or checks.
- lib/core/services/legion_control_client.dart, lib/core/theme/legion_accent.dart, and lib/core/widgets/{metric_format,metric_gauge,responsive_card_grid,surface_card}.dart: shortened abstract/design-history comments; retained units, null behavior, font source, fallback behavior in code, and layout constraints.
- Seven lib/features/analytics files: removed filename-only header comments that repeated their paths. No model schema or generated output changed.
- pubspec.yaml, analysis_options.yaml, .gitignore, linux/CMakeLists.txt, linux/runner/CMakeLists.txt: removed or shortened tutorial/template prose and fixed "resources must in the right relative locations". Non-comment values, ignore patterns, and build commands compare equal to HEAD.
- docs/model-support.md: "only the named model and BIOS fields" contradicted exported versions/probes/history. The guide now lists report contents and omitted fields; it still requires reviewing personal information before sharing.
- docs/architecture/sysfs-vs-cli-access-audit.md and overview.md: replaced removed repository names and Automation consumers with current callers; documented direct Settings service calls, Spectrum/OpenRGB lighting, discovered Mains readings, and complete-curve file counts. Marked the audit as representative rather than exhaustive, and removed the old monitor-task shorthand.
- docs/architecture/portable-control.md: "Desktop selection ... remain[s] open" contradicted implemented Settings. It now distinguishes qualification-build selection from unqualified release packages.
- README.md and BACKLOG.md: updated review dates and stale native persistence/restart gaps against existing integration journeys, without claiming new physical-device checks. CONTRIBUTING.md now wraps that journey description into readable sentences.

## Follow-ups outside this writing pass

- lllf-twi: discuss a coordinated rename of internal power-default fields/keys to references; no restoration or value changes.
- lllf-nnd: trace the driver fan-lock contract before adding a stronger explanation or changing its safety guidance; no hardware test without approval.
- lllf-6h9: measure existing Power helper-text contrast in the light theme before changing visual styles. Rendered copy fits, but screenshot inspection is not a measured contrast audit.

title: Show RGB profile application errors on Automation
description: Native profile-recovery work found lib/features/automation/view/automation_page.dart passes only AutomationBloc state.errorMessage into AppPageBody, while Apply current profile and runtime assignments dispatch RgbProfileLoaded to rgbLightingBlocProvider. An RGB apply failure is stored in the RGB Bloc but is not presented on Automation. Discuss a narrow shared-error-listener change, preserve typed errors and retry behavior, then add a native Automation apply/retry journey. Current native failure/retry coverage intentionally uses Lighting's existing visible-error path; it does not claim Automation failure feedback. Discovered in lllf-gcc.2.
notes:
User approved OpenRGB failure handling and Automation error feedback. Implemented injectable OpenRGB process boundary with typed commandFailed/unavailable errors and preserved command/exit/stdout/stderr diagnostics. Optional discovery still falls back to native Spectrum. Automation passes RGB errors through existing AppPageBody. OpenRGB manual color/mode/brightness state now changes after successful command completion; failed profile/manual writes preserve prior successful values and persisted config. Tests use real service/repository/Bloc with controlled ProcessResult completion, including retry. SafeLighting now fakes only process results, so native Lighting/Automation failure tests exercise actual exit classification. Replaced service comment 'buggy SDK socket package' (unsupported judgment) with concrete CLI purpose.
Native recovery tests exposed existing NavigationShell RGB error handling outside Lighting, which the original issue omitted. Automation page ownership must exclude the shell listener there to keep one dialog. Investigating repeated identical failures: AppErrorDialogListener compares built values, so a fast clear/fail retry may be coalesced before a frame. Keep the regression test; avoid inventing timestamps or weakening retry coverage.
Narrow retry fix: AppPageBody/AppErrorDialogListener accept an optional typed onErrorDismissed callback; RGB dispatches RgbErrorDismissed and clears only the identical displayed failure.
