title: Simplify project documentation
description:
User request: audit documentation and plan a plain-language rewrite. Audit completed against the current working tree; implementation is not started. Preserve existing edits in README.md, docs/README.md, and docs/architecture/overview.md.

Writing rules:
- Lead with what the reader needs to know or do.
- Delete sentences that add no useful instruction, explanation, or necessary warning. Do not merely shorten them.
- Use ordinary words and direct verbs; keep exact API names where needed.
- Put essential warnings beside the affected action. Keep detailed technical reasoning in reference sections.
- State a rule once and link to it elsewhere.
- Preserve commands, configuration, technical meaning, evidence, licensing requirements, and safety constraints.

Ordered implementation plan:
1. Entry points: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/README.md, docs/model-support.md. Shorten setup and contributor introductions, reduce vocabulary such as sanitized fixture and narrow boundary, simplify link labels, and replace the model-support opening with: Some features may not work on every model. Run diagnostics to find out why. README.md:76 should summarize read/write behavior and link to the architecture guide instead of explaining the full security design.
2. Architecture and setup: docs/architecture/overview.md, telemetry/README.md, docs/dependencies.md. Show the read/write flow directly, group service installation steps, replace retained compatibility boundaries and resolved graph with clear headings and wording. Keep package versions, compatibility reasons, and upgrade checks intact; consolidate repeated dependency-conflict explanations.
3. Contributor standards: docs/page-template.md and docs/error-and-feedback-standard.md. Consolidate repeated title/refresh, missing-data, accent, error, and success rules. Remove the repeated Do and Do Not summary where the existing checklist covers it. Separate user-facing error requirements from developer-only service details; do not require every error to explain internal security architecture. Keep concrete examples, code references, accessibility checks, and required security behavior.
4. Desktop integrations: docs/platform-surfaces.md, docs/platform-osd.md, docs/platform-tray.md, docs/platform-notifications.md. Lead with current availability. Replace unwired foundation, app-lifetime feature producers, implemented boundary, authoritative snapshot, and visual parity with direct descriptions. Split long paragraphs into usage, limitations, cleanup, and testing sections. Avoid repeating unavailable/not connected/unverified status throughout each document. Keep exact ownership and protocol contracts in reference sections.
5. Hardware guides and investigations: docs/architecture/next-boot-graphics.md, docs/architecture/m1cn-hardware-evidence.md, docs/architecture/poweroff-stall-investigation.md, docs/architecture/pipewire-logout-crash.md, docs/power-defaults-evidence.md, docs/architecture/sysfs-vs-cli-access-audit.md. Put current status and practical steps first; separate historical evidence from current instructions. next-boot-graphics.md:3-5 says not hardware-validated despite later successful boot results at :228-328; describe exactly what passed and what remains untested without expanding the support claim. Simplify headings such as unresolved failure boundary, remediation, and without promoting them to a preset. Remove self-congratulation such as consistent, principled split and This is correct and should be maintained from the access audit. Preserve evidence tables, source revisions, recovery steps, uncertainty about causes, and warnings against unsafe graphics operations. Record technical contradictions separately rather than silently changing behavior or treating an old investigation as current fact.
6. Attribution: assets/gpu_vendors/README.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; README license section. Simplify only explanatory prose. Preserve required license text, attribution, source links, trademark conditions, and unresolved redistribution requirements.

Verification:
- Read every changed document for unnecessary statements, not just difficult words.
- Confirm readers can find prerequisites, action, expected result, and recovery where relevant.
- Compare commands, configuration blocks, identifiers, evidence, and warnings before/after.
- Check relative links and anchors, and run git diff --check.
- Keep implementation and UI copy outside this documentation-only task unless separately requested.

Scope excludes vendored/design skill instructions, generated metadata, and license bodies. This issue records the update plan; no documentation has been rewritten.

title: Integrate native StatusNotifierItem quick actions
description:
Implement the StatusNotifierItem/AppIndicator and desktop-owned menu described in docs/platform-surfaces.md, with state/capability derived from existing power, fans, battery and lighting features. Bridge commands through existing confirmation and privileged service boundaries; handle startup, disposal, absent watcher, and Wayland/X11. Add integration tests and desktop validation.

## Start in tray and close to tray

`lllf-wc5` needs start-in-tray and close-to-tray. This issue provides the tray foundation for that behavior:

- Connect one `PlatformTray(DBusTrayTransport())` for the app lifetime.
- Expose `Open` and `Quit` menu actions. Open shows and focuses the main window. Quit exits through the normal window shutdown path and bypasses close-to-tray.
- Support a hidden startup mode. Keep the window hidden while the tray is prepared. If no tray host is available, show the window.
- Install a `YaruWindow.onClose` handler. When the tray is usable, hide the window and return `false` to cancel the close. Otherwise allow the close.
- Use `YaruWindow.ensureInitialized()` and its `hide()`/`show()` methods. Keep the app running while hidden.
- Leave the minimize button alone. Minimize continues to minimize the window normally.
- Check `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher.IsStatusNotifierHostRegistered` before treating the tray as usable for hidden startup or close-to-tray. Watcher registration alone does not prove a visible host.
- If the tray is lost while the window is hidden, show the window.
- Do not let close-to-tray block session logout or shutdown. Exit normally on session end.
- Keep privileged hardware actions behind the existing confirmation flow. Do not add a tray action that changes hardware while the window is hidden without confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One app-lifetime tray registers with an available watcher and exposes the designed menu.
- The app can start with its window hidden and the tray active when a StatusNotifier host is registered. No window flash occurs.
- Without a host, hidden startup shows the window and close exits normally.
- Closing the window hides it to the tray and keeps the app running when a host is registered.
- The minimize button still minimizes the window normally and does not hide it to the tray.
- Open shows and focuses the window; Quit exits the app and bypasses the close-to-tray handler.
- Tray loss while hidden restores the window.
- Session logout and shutdown exit the app normally; close-to-tray does not block them.
- Quick actions use confirmed state and the existing confirmation and privileged service boundaries.
- Tests cover watcher absence, host absence, registration, hidden startup, menu activation, the close handler, minimize remaining normal, disposal, and tray loss while hidden.
- Desktop validation on KDE Wayland records start-in-tray, close-to-tray, normal minimize, Open, and Quit. Record X11 or other desktops when checked.
- `docs/platform-tray.md` describes the connected behavior, the host-registration limit, and the desktop overflow-menu limitation.

title: Triage LLT hardening lessons and low-priority parity ideas
description:
Capture the review criteria and low-priority ideas from the LLT v2.38 comparison so they are not lost.

Low-priority parity ideas:
- CPU temperature source selection when hwmon exposes several plausible sources.
- AC/DC and time-based automation triggers. Do not add arbitrary script or program execution; keep the current keyboard-profile scope until a separate decision.
- Settings backup, restore, and reset for the app's Hive data, with validation and clear overwrite behavior.

Review criteria to apply to new feature work:
- Verify requested values before reporting success, including accepted-but-clamped and missing-readback cases.
- Preserve user drafts and saved settings when verification fails.
- Prefer capability-driven UI over per-model assumptions.
- Do not clear unrelated preferences when a backend is unavailable.
- Retry a sensor after a failed read instead of permanently dropping it.
- Scope sampling to visible surfaces and dispose subscriptions when hidden.
- Handle multi-monitor, DPI, and session-lock behavior explicitly.
- Defer disk saves until a drag ends; keep expensive reads and allocations off the UI thread.

Housekeeping: refresh docs/power-defaults-evidence.md when lllf-dok or lllf-zfg reopens; it still cites LLT 31d0db27 and the removed GodModeControllerV3.
acceptance_criteria: Each low-priority idea is triaged or linked to a concrete issue, or explicitly deferred with a reason. The hardening criteria are recorded in the appropriate review guidance or issue comments. The stale LLT reference is scheduled for the next power-defaults update. title: Validate boot logo dimensions and real format before privileged upload
description:
LLT detects the real file format, checks dimensions, and prepares the image before touching the EFI partition (LenovoLegionToolkit.Lib/System/BootLogo.cs, commit 646d47a6). Our UI only checks the filename extension in lib/features/boot_logo/bloc/boot_logo_bloc.dart, so a wrong-size or renamed image fails later inside the privileged upload. The Linux backend already validates exact dimensions and format.

Work:
- On file selection, read the real format from file content and read the image dimensions.
- Compare them with BootLogoStatus.requiredWidth/requiredHeight.
- Show expected versus actual size and a clear recovery step before the user confirms.
- Do not send a known-invalid file to the privileged path.
- Do not silently resize or rewrite the user's image. If we want LLT-like convenience, offer a separate explicit action and keep the original.
- Use a small header parser or the existing Flutter codec where possible; avoid adding an image library just for this.

Tests: PNG, JPEG, and BMP; renamed files; truncated or malformed files; wrong and unknown dimensions; missing boot-logo status.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid dimensions or format are rejected before the privileged upload with expected and actual details. Valid files still reach the existing upload path. No image is silently modified. Tests cover the listed formats and failure cases.

title: Refresh dGPU state after sleep and power cycles
description:
LLT v2.38 re-applies GPU settings after sleep, display wake, and power-mode changes, and treats a dGPU that is not powered as a normal state rather than an error (commits 5c1650ec, 812203f1, 0bb32908). Our dGPU code currently polls while the page is open but should explicitly distinguish asleep or unavailable from failed.

Work:
- Refresh selected and effective graphics state, PCI runtime status, and process state after resume and after a GPU power-cycle.
- Do not surface a transient not-powered state as a failure or clear saved settings.
- Re-read authoritative state before enabling actions; keep the existing confirmation and baseline checks.
- Do not copy LLT's NVAPI overclock, voltage, or P-State controls. Our firmware-backed overclock toggle has a different contract.

Related: lllf-h69, lllf-j9t.6.
acceptance_criteria: Resume and power-cycle fixtures or tests show the dGPU returning to a refreshed, actionable state. A not-powered GPU is reported as unavailable, not failed. No saved setting is cleared, and no stale state enables an action. Hardware evidence remains separate.

title: Review LLT lighting changes for next lighting work
description:
Review these LLT v2.38 lighting changes during the next lighting pass. Do not implement them blindly.

- ISO/JIS per-key layouts: LLT detects the layout and stops a stored ANSI layout from overriding a detected ISO/JIS layout (3e2379db), and serializes rapid layout switches (da6be8ec). Our native profile is ANSI-only; tracked separately.
- One-zone and 24-zone Spectrum are built in on LLT. Our native backend targets 048d:c987 per-key; OpenRGB covers other devices. Do not add native one-zone/24-zone support without a protocol source and hardware evidence.
- Keyboard type from Lighting_Type bits 1-3: LLT fixed per-key keyboards falling back to one-zone control when firmware reports no type (a296bce3, ed645720). Check whether our HID discovery and diagnostics can represent that ambiguity.
- Effect support gating: LLT hides effects unsupported by the keyboard type. Our software effects may not need firmware gating, but the UI must not claim firmware effects the device lacks.
- Random/custom color and idle/lock interactions: LLT added color selection and OSD session-lock behavior. Consider only if they fit our profile and effect model.
acceptance_criteria: Each item is triaged as adopt, defer, or reject with evidence. Concrete work links to a task. No new native device protocol is added without a recorded device and test fixture.

title: Support ISO/JIS Spectrum layouts or state ANSI-only
description:
Our native per-key Spectrum profile uses OpenRGB's ANSI LED table and kLegionAnsiLayout (lib/features/lighting/models/spectrum_keyboard_profile.dart and keyboard_layout.dart). A user with an ISO or JIS 048d:c987 keyboard can paint the wrong physical keys. LLT fixed stored ANSI layouts overriding detected ISO/JIS layouts and serialized rapid layout switches (commits 3e2379db and da6be8ec).

Immediate action: document that native Spectrum mapping is ANSI-only unless we add layouts, and expose the layout in diagnostics and model-support guidance. Do not guess ISO/JIS maps.

If support is added:
- Choose a manual layout setting or a verified detection source.
- Add ISO/JIS LED maps and preview layouts from a pinned source.
- Persist the selection and serialize rapid changes.
- Test with synthetic maps and a real device; keep hardware evidence separate.
- Keep OpenRGB as the fallback for keyboards we do not support natively.
acceptance_criteria: The ANSI-only limitation is documented and visible in diagnostics. If ISO/JIS support is implemented, preview and painting are correct on a verified device, rapid switches are serialized, tests use synthetic maps, and hardware evidence is recorded separately.

title: Review LLT v2.38 parity and hardening follow-ups
description:
Comparison baseline: LenovoLegionToolkit 31d0db27..ab16eb1b (v2.38.0.0, 801 commits). Most of the diff is Windows-only. This epic records the parts worth considering for the Linux frontend: lighting behavior, platform surfaces, fan verification and identity, dGPU state after sleep, window and tray behavior, boot-logo validation, and low-priority parity ideas.

Children carry concrete work. Existing issues receive comments where the work already has an owner. Do not port NVAPI overclocking, voltage/P-State controls, Windows power plans, HDR/ACM/DRR, software disablers, the script console, or the plugin system without a separate Linux contract and approval.

Engineering lessons recorded here:
- Verify requested values before reporting success.
- Preserve user drafts and saved settings when verification fails.
- Prefer capability-driven UI over per-model assumptions.
- Availability changes must not clear unrelated preferences.
- One failed sensor read is not a dead sensor; retry on the next update.
- Scope sensor sampling to visible surfaces and dispose subscriptions when hidden.
- Handle multi-monitor, DPI, and session-lock behavior explicitly.
- Defer disk saves until a drag completes; keep expensive reads off the UI thread.

Low-priority ideas: CPU temperature source selection, AC/DC and time-based automation triggers without arbitrary script execution, and settings backup/restore/reset. Revisit only after current verification and packaging work.

Housekeeping: docs/power-defaults-evidence.md still cites LLT 31d0db27 and the removed GodModeControllerV3. LLT's current data-driven GodMode configuration still uses explicit capability DefaultValue/min/max/step, so the conclusion holds. Refresh the reference when reopening lllf-dok or lllf-zfg.
acceptance_criteria: Each child is triaged or closed with evidence. Existing issue comments link the relevant LLT commits. No Windows-only control is added without a Linux contract. Low-priority items stay deferred until current priorities clear.
